newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks edge up at close after fickle trade.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks edge up at close after fickle trade.

text.p: Mexican stocks closed up on Tuesday after a low-volume session in which prices were swayed both up and down by relatively small trades, dealers said.

"The market showed no clear trends today. Dealers were obviously still awaiting the outcome of the main forthcoming foreign event, the Federal Open Market Committee meeting tomorrow," said Santos Herrera, analyst at the Estrategia Bursatil brokerage.
The blue chip IPC index closed up 4.7 points, or 0.14 percent, at 3,374.42. Volume was 90.3 million shares, but one third of that was due to cross trades, dealers noted.
The IPC reached a low of 3,353.78 during the session.
"Dealers may also be wary of the high levels the Dow Jones has reached, and suspect that it may adjust downwards, which would hurt us," Herrera added.
The Dow Jones meanwhile ended up 10.44 points, or 0.17 percent, at a record close of 6,266.04.
Dealers also said they had discounted primary Cetes auction results, due later in the day.
A Reuters survey showed an average forecast of 29.66 percent for benchmark 27-day Cetes rates, or 21 basis points above last week's rate.
On the broad market scoreboard, 112 stocks changed hands, with gainers outnumbering losers by 43 to 39.
Food company Maizoro headed the leaders, up 20 centavos at 3.00 pesos, on a favorable outlook for the company's exports, traders said.
The only percentage loser traded at appreciable volume was financial stock BBVPro, down one centavo to 45.
Technical analysts said the bourse was consolidating in order to gather steam to break out of the 3,400 point mark.
